newsitem.title: ITALY: Italcementi eyes Far East, south America.
newsitem.headline: Italcementi eyes Far East, south America.

text.p: Italy's Italcementi Group, the largest cement producer in the European Union, is eyeing expansion opportunities in the Far East and south America to add to its strength in Europe and north America.
Italcementi, which acquired Ciment Francais some five years ago, is now to integrate fully the French cement maker.

"It will be a major integration, there are no merger plans and no plans for quotation in other bourses. But in the future, I do not exclude these," the group's chairman, Giampaolo Pesenti, said on Monday evening.

Currently, Italcementi has a strong presence in Europe and the U.S., "markets that have reached maturity and show reduced growth rates....while the Far East and South America interest us," said Pesenti.

Earlier this year in February, Italcementi reported consolidated 1996 sales slipping to 5.14 trillion lire from 5.47 trillion lire in 1995, while its gross operating margin was 27 percent. The company's board will examine the full 1996 results in the first half of May.

At the same time in February, Italcementi bought Calcestruzzi SpA, the Italian concrete interests of Italian financial holding Compart, but Italcementi said it had no intention of acquired Compart's remaining Greek cement businesses.
Compart said that its holding group Calcemento was selling off its concrete interests as Calcestruzzi, but Calcemento will continue to hold Compart's Greek building product interests.
